summary.tldr: Allows jurors and some people who support them to share jury information with health care professionals for treatment, therapy, or counselling after a trial.
what_it_does: Keeps it an offence for jurors and people who support a juror with a disability to disclose jury information that was not said in open court.
Adds an exception that allows that information to be shared with a health care professional for medical or psychiatric treatment, therapy, or counselling after the trial.
Limits that health care exception to professionals who are allowed to practise under provincial law.
Keeps other exceptions for investigations and criminal proceedings about an alleged offence under section 139(2).
who_it_affects: People who support jurors with disabilities
summary.background: Section 649 of the Criminal Code currently bans disclosure of jury proceedings outside the courtroom. This bill replaces that section and adds a new exception for certain health-related disclosure.
